symptoms: database does not match expected state
runbooks.diagnosis: Zitadel runs config/setup migrations against postgres at startup. A failed migration is usually a schema lock left by a killed previous setup container, or an unreachable postgres DSN (wrong host/db in ZITADEL_DATABASE_POSTGRES_HOST).
remediation: Check zitadel-setup logs for the failing step
Verify postgres is reachable from the zitadel network
Remove stale advisory locks only if no setup container is running
Re-run the setup step after the blocker is cleared

runbooks.diagnosis: The service's OIDC redirect URI registered in Zitadel does not match the externally visible URL. Happens when the public domain or Traefik router rule changed after the client was provisioned.
remediation: Compare the callback URL in the Zitadel project's app config with the service's external URL
Update the redirect URI in Zitadel (or the service's OIDC env) — they must match byte-for-byte
No restart needed; Zitadel applies client changes immediately

runbooks.diagnosis: Zitadel startup probe flaps while postgres is still migrating or under connection pressure from the other services starting in parallel.
remediation: Wait for postgres healthy before restarting zitadel
Raise the healthcheck start_period instead of restarting

symptoms: admin password invalid after fresh provisioning
password is invalid on fresh zitadel
runbooks.diagnosis: Zitadel v3.4 silently IGNORES unknown FIRSTINSTANCE env keys. ZITADEL_FIRSTINSTANCE_USERADMIN_* (and other older names) are dead — the instance then seeds zitadel's built-in default admin (userName zitadel-admin@zitadel.<domain>, random password) instead of the intended one. Only ZITADEL_FIRSTINSTANCE_ORG_* keys work (verify against `strings` of the binary). Complexity policy at seed time comes from ZITADEL_DEFAULTINSTANCE_PASSWORDCOMPLEXITYPOLICY_* — a .env password without a symbol needs HASSYMBOL: false or setup fails with PasswordComplexityPolicy.HasSymbol.
remediation: Set ORG_HUMAN_PASSWORDCHANGEREQUIRED: false — a forced first-login pw change breaks headless automation (CSRF tokens are single-use, /ui/login/password/change is POST-only)
Login name is username@<orgdomain>.<instancedomain> — the org domain comes from ORG_NAME, not from the admin email
Full re-provision: stop/rm zitadel, DROP DATABASE zitadel WITH (FORCE), compose run zitadel init, compose run zitadel setup --masterkeyFile /secrets/masterkey, up -d

symptoms: machine user has no personal access token
runbooks.diagnosis: ZITADEL_FIRSTINSTANCE_PATPATH does not reliably write the seeded machine user's PAT file to the volume in v3.4. Mint one via the Management API instead — note the v3.4 route is /management/v1/users/{userId}/pats (PLURAL; the old /pat returns a bare 404 {code:5}).
remediation: Login as admin (PKCE dance or console), POST /management/v1/users/{userId}/pats with Bearer token
Write the token into the machinekey volume (e.g. _data/pat, mode 600) where services expect it
Verify: GET /management/v1/users/{userId} with Authorization: Bearer <pat> → 200 (users/me does NOT work for machine users)
